title: Cohort-based Embedding Drift Reconciliation Playbook
author: Ravi Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook defines a repeatable, low-risk procedure to detect, triage, and reconcile embedding drift at the cohort level. It is targeted at product teams, ML infra, and SREs who operate embedding services (search, semantic retrieval, recommendation) and want to maintain semantic parity across model, quantization, and data drift events.

Scope and motivation

- Scope: production embedding services (hosted + dedicated) that provide vector embeddings to downstream search/recall pipelines.
- Motivation: global drift signals can be noisy; cohort-level monitoring isolates affected user segments and reduces false positives. Reconciliation aims to restore utility (precision/recall, nearest-neighbor stability) with minimal user-facing regressions.

Definitions

- Cohort: a stable grouping of traffic by attributes (tenant, locale, client-version, feature-flag). Cohorts must be defined in the Cohort Registry (see Operational Configurations).
- Drift signal: a statistically significant change in embedding distribution or downstream retrieval performance relative to baseline.
- Reconciliation: interventions to bring cohort behavior back within SLA (can include prompt rewriting, model rollback, re-embedding, quant-profile change, or routing to fallback model).

Detection and alerting

1) Telemetry to collect per-request:
   - embedding vector summary stats (L2 norm, mean, std)
   - cosine similarity to pinned baselines and per-cohort centroid
   - retrieval metrics: top-k precision@k, rerank delta, latency, token count
   - cache hit ratio and kv-cache invalidation events

2) Aggregation cadence and windowing:
   - Primary aggregation: 15m windows for high-volume cohorts, 1H for low-volume.
   - Baseline comparison windows: 7d rolling baseline and 28d seasonal baseline.

3) Statistical tests and thresholds (configurable defaults):
   - Embedding distribution shift: Wasserstein distance > 0.12 and mean L2 change > 0.08 => warning.
   - Similarity shift: median cosine-to-centroid drop > 0.06 => warning.
   - Downstream signal: precision@10 drop > 4% absolute => critical.

4) Alerting rules:
   - Warning alert: any single metric breach on 2 consecutive windows.
   - Critical alert: any downstream precision or recall breach OR three distinct metric classes breached in single window.
   - Alert destinations: cohort-owner Slack channel, eval-oncall rotation, and incident ticket created in P1 queue.

Cohort triage workflow (high level)

1) Triage intake (automated):
   - Auto-attach cohort telemetry snapshot (last 3 windows), baseline diffs, and representative probe queries to the incident ticket.

2) Initial human validation (5–20 min):
   - Owner verifies cohort definition and checks recent deploys, quantization promotions, routing changes, and data schema changes.
   - If a deploy or quant promotion correlates to the first breach timestamp, tag the deploy-id and escalate to rollout lead.

3) Quick impact check (15–45 min):
   - Run cohort smoke eval: sample N=200 representative queries and compute precision@10, MRR, and embedding similarity distribution.
   - If precision@10 drop > 6% and reproduced locally, proceed to Reconciliation Plan.

Reconciliation plan (ordered by risk and time-to-restore)

The reconciliation plan provides a prioritized list of mitigations. Always prefer low-risk, reversible actions first.

Low-risk / Fast (minutes):
- Route cohort to warm fallback model (same architecture but previous model version) using routing policy: route 100% traffic for cohort to fallback.
- Increase caching TTL and enable cohort-specific prefix caching to preserve previous embeddings while rollback is underway.
- Apply prompt-layer (client-side) soft rewrite to reduce sensitive tokens known to cause representation shifts.

Medium-risk / Moderate (tens of minutes–hours):
- Quantization rollback: revert quant profile for cohort to previous profile and promote via canary rule for cohort traffic.
- Re-embed a short tail of recent documents (select 48–72h window) observed in the cohort with the baseline model.
- Apply feature flag to use hybrid nearest-neighbor scoring (combine new embeddings score * 0.7 + persisted-score * 0.3).

High-risk / Heavy (hours–days):
- Full model rollback for cohort (requires SLA signoff).
- Recompute corpus-wide embeddings for cohorted data and run data consistency verification pipeline.

Example reconciliation decision matrix (text table)

| Symptom | Immediate action | Escalation threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Precision@10 drop 4-6% | Route 100% to fallback model for cohort | Not resolved in 30m | Cohort owner |
| Median cosine drop 0.06-0.12 | Increase cache TTL + start re-embed job for hot docs | Downstream metrics degrade | ML infra lead |
| Precision@10 drop >6% or memnorm shift >0.2 | Promote quant rollback + hybrid scoring | Requires model rollback | Platform SRE and ML lead |

Operational configurations (required fields)

Provide the following entries per cohort in the Cohort Registry YAML. Example YAML snippet:

cohort_id: "tenant-42-us-v2"
owner: "team-search"
definition:
  - attribute: "tenant_id"
    match: "42"
  - attribute: "client_version"
    match: ">=2.0"
baseline_window: "7d"
aggregation_cadence: "15m"
sample_size_smoke_eval: "200"
fallback_model: "embedding-model-v3.1"
preferred_quant_profile: "q8_legacy"
notify_channels:
  - "#tenant-42-search"
  - "eval-oncall"

Integration with eval harness and probes

- Every cohort must have an associated probe-set (N>=500 probes recommended) annotated with expected semantics and golden retrieval targets. The probe-set is used for smoke evaluation and for regression repro.
- The eval harness will expose a per-cohort reproducibility job: a single-command re-run that snapshots current model outputs and computes the metrics.

CLI example (repro job):

redwood-eval run --cohort tenant-42-us-v2 --probe-set tenant-42-core --snapshot-id auto --metrics precision@10,MRR,cosine_median

Acceptance criteria for reconciliation rollout

- Primary acceptance: precision@10 within 1% absolute of baseline across a 24h window post-action and median cosine similarity restored to within 0.02 of baseline.
- Secondary acceptance: end-to-end latency impact < 10% and token-cost delta < 5% compared to baseline.
- Postmortem requirement: if any action required model rollback or re-embed > 24h, a 72h postmortem with root cause analysis and remediation timeline must be authored.

Observability and dashboards

Minimum dashboard panels per cohort:
- Embedding norm distribution (heatmap) with baseline overlay.
- Median cosine-to-centroid time series vs baseline.
- Precision@k and MRR time series with deploy and quant-change annotations.
- Active re-embed job queue length and estimated time to completion.

Retention and privacy considerations

- Per-cohort probes and telemetry snapshots are retained for 90 days. For cohorts tied to regulated datasets, store only derived statistics and anonymized probe identifiers; raw inputs must be excluded unless data access is approved.

Roles and responsibilities

- Cohort owner: primary triage and initial reconciliation decision.
- ML infra: quant rollback, re-embed orchestration, rerouting policies.
- Platform SRE: implement routing changes, monitor latency and cost.
- Eval-oncall: run smoke evals and validate reproducibility.

Runbook: step-by-step (abridged)

1) Receive alert and confirm cohort definition in Cohort Registry.
2) Attach 3-window telemetry snapshot and run single-command smoke eval.
3) If smoke eval reproduces degradation, apply low-risk routing fallback for cohort.
4) Monitor metrics for 30m; if improvement, plan medium-risk action (quant rollback or re-embed).
5) If unresolved or worsening, convene incident bridge and assess model rollback.
6) After restore, open postmortem and tag related deploy/quant assets for follow-up.

Appendices

A. Typical thresholds rationale
- Wasserstein & cosine thresholds derived from historical false-positive curve analysis (see related baseline notebook). They are intentionally conservative for low-volume cohorts.

B. Example alert payload (JSON)
{
  "cohort_id": "tenant-42-us-v2",
  "window_start": "2026-03-02T10:15:00Z",
  "metrics": {
    "cosine_median": 0.72,
    "cosine_baseline": 0.80,
    "precision@10": 0.61,
    "precision_baseline": 0.68
  },
  "breaches": ["precision@10", "cosine_median"],
  "suggested_action": "route_fallback_model"
}

Contact and escalation matrix

- Primary: Cohort owner (on-call)
- Secondary: ML Infra (pager)
- Tertiary: Platform SRE Lead
